title: The Signal Room: Vector Databases, Part One
summary: Opened the episode and framed the question: what a vector database is actually for, and why exact-match indexes were the wrong tool for similarity search.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Welcome to The Signal Room. We've got a long one today, because vector search is one of those topics where the summary version is actively misleading.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: It is. People hear database and picture rows and a WHERE clause, and that mental model falls apart immediately.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Because you're not asking for a match, you're asking for nearness.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Nearness in a few hundred dimensions, which our intuitions are terrible at. A B-tree gives you nothing here. There's no ordering to exploit.

title: The Signal Room: Vector Databases, Part Two
summary: Covered approximate nearest neighbour indexes, the recall-versus-latency trade-off, and why HNSW became the default choice.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So if you can't index it the usual way, what replaced the B-tree?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Approximate nearest neighbour structures. HNSW is the one most people end up on — a layered graph where you greedily walk toward your query.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: You give up a guarantee of the exact top results for something that returns in single-digit milliseconds. And you tune that knowingly — recall against latency, and you should be measuring recall, not assuming it.

title: The Signal Room: Vector Databases, Part Three
summary: Closed on operational realities: re-embedding costs when the model changes, filtering interacting badly with the index, and a wrap-up.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Before we wrap, the thing nobody warns you about: what happens when you change embedding models?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: You re-embed everything. The old vectors are meaningless in the new space. That's a migration, and on a large corpus it's a real one.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And metadata filtering, which people assume is free.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: It fights the index. Filter hard enough and the graph walk can't find enough candidates, so recall quietly collapses. Test it with your real filters, not a synthetic benchmark.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Good place to stop. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you next week.
